Clinical Trigger Event

On March 24, 2026, the ED team managed a difficult airway case involving a 58-year-old male MVA patient with facial trauma and suspected C-spine injury. The patient required emergent intubation with GCS 8, but significant challenges were encountered due to limited neck mobility, poor oropharyngeal visualization, and equipment limitations with our current video laryngoscope.

The case required three intubation attempts over 8 minutes, ultimately successful with bougie assistance. While the clinical outcome was favorable, the M&M conference review on March 26 identified critical equipment deficiencies that compromised optimal patient care.
Evaluation Process
Following the M&M conference, an equipment evaluation committee was formed to assess video laryngoscope options. The evaluation considered:

items: Image quality and screen visibility in ED lighting conditions
Blade variety and availability for diverse patient populations
Long-term cost analysis (initial purchase + maintenance/consumables)
Training requirements for resident education
Clinical performance in difficult airway scenarios
Budget constraints (target range ¥40,000-50,000)

blocks.text: Options Considered
**Option A: GlideScope AVL (Verathon)** - ¥45,000 initial cost, reusable blades, excellent optics, minimal maintenance (¥3,000/year). Five-year total cost: ¥60,000.
**Option B: McGrath MAC (Medtronic) newer model** - ¥38,000 initial cost, disposable blades (¥180 each, ~140 difficult airways/year = ¥25,000 annually). Five-year total cost: ¥138,000.
**Option C: King Vision (Ambu)** - ¥32,000 initial cost, but inferior image quality and limited blade options. Not recommended for high-acuity ED environment.
Discussion Summary
The decision was finalized in the ed-general Mattermost channel on March 31, 2026, following comprehensive evaluation and stakeholder input. Key discussion points included:

items: Dr. Wang Li recommended GlideScope based on previous institutional experience and superior clinical performance
Anesthesia department consultation confirmed GlideScope as gold standard for difficult airways
Resident feedback indicated both GlideScope and McGrath were acceptable, with slight ergonomic preference for GlideScope
Cost-benefit analysis strongly favored GlideScope over 5-year lifecycle (¥78,000 savings vs McGrath)
Equipment durability and reusable blade system reduce long-term operational costs

blocks.text: Final Decision
**APPROVED: GlideScope AVL Video Laryngoscope System with Reusable Blades (Adult Set)**

**Rationale**: The GlideScope AVL offers the best combination of clinical performance, long-term cost-effectiveness, and educational value for our high-acuity ED environment. Superior optics and blade durability address the specific equipment limitations identified in the March 24 difficult airway case.
Budget Impact
**Initial Investment**: ¥45,000 (within approved Q1 equipment budget allocation)
**Annual Maintenance**: ¥3,000 (blade sterilization, system calibration)
**Five-Year Total Cost of Ownership**: ¥60,000
**Budget Source**: ED Quality Improvement Equipment Fund (approved by Dr. Chen, ED Director)
